01 / About

A QA engineer who reads between the requirements.

Profile Summary

Detail-oriented Software QA Engineer and Business Analyst with over 4 years of experience analyzing business processes, documenting workflows, and ensuring software quality across web, mobile, and desktop applications. Skilled at collaborating with cross-functional teams to gather requirements, map end-to-end workflows, identify process inefficiencies, and create clear documentation that supports process improvement and future automation.

Experienced in manual testing, API testing, user acceptance testing (UAT), defect tracking, and business process analysis using tools such as Jira, ClickUp, Postman, and TestRail. Adept at translating complex business requirements into structured workflows, test cases, and functional documentation while maintaining a strong focus on accuracy and continuous improvement.

A proactive problem-solver with excellent analytical, communication, and organizational skills who enjoys learning how businesses operate and transforming ambiguous processes into well-defined, efficient systems. Passionate about helping organizations optimize operations through process analysis, quality assurance, and workflow documentation.

I started on the other side of the ticket — as an Associate Software Engineer at Accenture, resolving defects and building the systems other people would later test. That's shaped how I approach QA now: I'm not just checking boxes, I'm thinking about what the developer might have missed and what the requirements doc didn't quite say.

Since then I've tested patient records and billing workflows for a Healthcare Management System, secure login and account-recovery flows for SaaS platforms, and game mechanics under deadline for two commercial titles at Mega Cat Studio. Each domain teaches you to look for a different kind of failure — a healthcare system can't afford a wrong appointment date; a game can't afford a broken combo under load.

I work manual-first and am steadily building an automation practice with Playwright, and I recently completed Microsoft's Azure AI Fundamentals training — because testing is starting to lean on AI-assisted tools, and I'd rather be ready for that shift than catch up to it later.

02 / What I Do

Testing coverage that goes beyond the checklist.

Ten overlapping disciplines I move between depending on what a release actually needs.

Manual Testing

Hands-on testing to catch functional, usability, and experience issues before they reach a release.

Functional Testing

Validating that every feature does exactly what the requirements say it should — nothing assumed.

Regression Testing

Re-verifying existing functionality after every change, so yesterday's fix doesn't become tomorrow's bug.

Exploratory Testing

Testing without a script — probing the product the way a curious, occasionally mischievous user would.

API Testing

Validating REST endpoints in Postman — status codes, request/response shape, auth, and error handling.

Automation Testing

Building repeatable Playwright coverage for the flows that matter most, so manual testing time goes further.

Performance & Stress Testing

Pushing builds under load and edge-case conditions to see where they bend before they break.

UAT & Business Analysis

Translating business requirements into technical specs, then confirming the finished product actually meets them.

Usability Testing

Evaluating how intuitive and easy a product feels for real users — not just whether it technically works.

Smoke Testing

A fast pass/fail check on a new build before deeper testing begins — is it stable enough to test at all?

03 / How I Work

A repeatable process for reliable releases.

The same eight-step cycle, whether the release is a healthcare module or a game patch.

01

Analyze Requirements

Read the spec — and what it leaves out — to understand what "working" actually means.

  • Review the BRD (Business Requirements Document)
  • Review user stories
  • Review acceptance criteria
  • Clarify missing or ambiguous requirements
  • Identify business risk
02

Test Planning

Scope coverage, priorities, and approach before a single test case is written.

03

Test Case Design

Turn requirements into clear, repeatable cases — happy paths and edge cases both.

04

Test Execution

Run the suite manually or via Playwright, tracking results as I go.

05

Defect Reporting

Log clear, reproducible defects in JIRA or Mantis — steps, evidence, severity.

06

Retesting

Confirm each fix actually resolves the issue that was reported.

07

Regression Testing

Make sure the fix — and everything around it — still works as expected.

08

Test Closure

Summarize coverage and outstanding risk, and sign off with confidence.
